**1. Stale comments adjacent to changed lines.**
Found one, real: the test file's header docstring said fixtures "are built with them in `beforeAll`" — false, they're built by `buildFixtureLesson()` called from each test body; `beforeAll` only ever probed ffmpeg. **Fixed** (rewrote the paragraph to describe what actually happens and why the check has to run at module load). Everything else I re-read — the exporter's module docstring, `EXPORT_STATES`, `MIN_SLIDE_SECONDS`, `_blank_frame`'s comment, the exit-code list — still accurately describes the code beside it.

**2. Something left with nothing reaching it.**
Found one, real: `describe.skipIf(!ffmpegAvailable)` read a flag that was only ever mutated inside `beforeAll`, which vitest runs *after* it evaluates `skipIf` at collection time. I verified this isn't theoretical — built a two-line repro (`beforeAll` flips a flag from `true`→`false`, `skipIf` reads it) and the gated test still ran. So the guard was dead: it could never actually skip, regardless of whether ffmpeg was present. It also only wrapped one of the three describes that all depend on ffmpeg via `buildFixtureLesson`. **Fixed**: computed `ffmpegAvailable` synchronously at module load (before any `describe` registers) and applied it to all three describes.

**3. Never-asked / found-nothing / failed, for each resource read.**
`deck.json` (always required, unreadable/malformed → `ExportFailed`, loud), `manifest.json` and the prior `video-manifest.json` (absent → distinct default value; present-but-corrupt → `ExportFailed`, never silently read as absent), and the `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` subprocess calls (non-zero exit → `ExportFailed` with stderr, never a swallowed failure). All three states are distinguished at every read; no criterion here maps to only two. No finding.

**4. Red-proof file, read directly.** All four `observed` blocks are `AssertionError: expected X to be/equal Y` lines — genuine assertion failures on the criterion's own claim, not import/build/collection errors. None empty. I also re-verified AC5 after editing its test body (strengthening it, see below) with a fresh mutation (`EXPORT_STATES` dropped `"stale"`) and got the same shape of real assertion failure, then reverted and confirmed green.

**5. The one sibling missing what the others have.**
Found one, real: the AC5 "three distinct values" test asserted against a hardcoded JS array (`["not-exported","current","stale"]`) with no connection to the script's actual output — unlike its sibling pattern in `generatedDeck.test.ts` ("three segment states... declared on the manifest itself"), and unlike every other AC5 case in this file, which all call the real script. A bug renaming/duplicating a state in `EXPORT_STATES` would have passed silently. **Fixed**: it now runs a real export and asserts against `video-manifest.json`'s own `schema.states`.

All three fixes are in `src/domain/script/data/videoExport.test.ts`, inside my `covers`. Re-ran all three of the task's verify commands after: `py_compile` passes, vitest 9/9 green, biome clean on `scripts src/domain/script/data`. Committed as `1b56cc08`.
